summary: A consultant-level look at invasive fungal infection on ICU. In EMPIRICUS (JAMA 2016, 260 patients), empirical micafungin for ICU-acquired sepsis with multisite Candida colonisation and multi-organ failure did not improve fungal-infection-free survival at day 28 (68% vs 60.2%, HR 1.35, 95% CI 0.87 to 2.08), although it reduced new proven infection (3% vs 12%). The 2016 Cochrane review found no mortality benefit from untargeted antifungals (RR 0.93). In CandiSep (ICM 2022, 339 patients), starting antifungals on a beta-D-glucan of 80 pg/mL or more got treatment in faster but did not reduce 28-day mortality (33.7% vs 30.5%). FUNDICU 2024 left BDG out of its research definition of probable deep-seated candidiasis. Two small single-centre trials (Rouzé 2017, De Pascale 2020) suggest that stopping on a negative biomarker safely shortens empirical therapy. Echinocandins remain first line. In ReSTORE (Lancet 2023), weekly rezafungin was non-inferior to caspofungin; the MHRA approved it in January 2024. Influenza-associated aspergillosis affected 19% of patients with severe influenza on ICU (Schauwvlieghe 2018) and is linked to high mortality. CAPA affected about 15% of ICU COVID patients in the ECMM study. POSA-FLU's prophylaxis trial was inconclusive. Diagnosis rests on lavage galactomannan (index of 1.0 or more), because serum galactomannan is insensitive in non-neutropenic patients. Treatment is voriconazole or isavuconazole, per ESCMID-ECMM-ERS 2017, IDSA 2016, the CAPA consensus and the Swiss FUNGINOS and German AWMF ICU guidelines of 2025. UKHSA's 2025 Candidozyma auris guidance covers admission screening, isolation and contact de-isolation, and says not to treat colonisation and to use an echinocandin first line; C. auris has been notifiable in England since 6 April 2025. Candidaemia is treated for 14 days after clearance, with step-down to an oral azole after 5 to 7 days (IDSA 2016) or at least 5 days (global ECMM/ISHAM/ASM guideline 2025) in stable patients.
takeaways: Don't start empirical echinocandins for colonisation and sepsis alone: EMPIRICUS and CandiSep showed no survival benefit. Treat septic shock with a real Candida risk, and reassess by day 4 to 5.
Use beta-D-glucan to stop antifungals rather than to start them: a negative result supports stopping, but a positive one is non-specific.
In severe influenza and COVID, look for aspergillus early with lavage galactomannan (serum is insensitive), and treat with voriconazole or isavuconazole.

Candida (Candidozyma) auris has been notifiable in England since April 2025. Screen patients admitted after healthcare abroad, isolate or cohort them, and don't treat colonisation. Use an echinocandin for infection.
For candidaemia, remove the line early, treat for 14 days from clearance, and step down to fluconazole after about 5 days in stable patients with susceptible isolates and negative repeat cultures.
